{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint timepoint inconsistency",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint will be evaluated at week 18.",
      "page": 6,
      "section": "4.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The synopsis states the primary endpoint is evaluated at week 18, but the primary endpoint definition in the endpoints section says 'percent change in EASI score from baseline to week 16'. This discrepancy could lead to analysis errors.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether the primary endpoint is measured at week 16 or week 18 and align all sections."
    },
    {
      "title": "Incomplete treatment regimen description for 30 mg Q8W",
      "quote": "REGN3500 30 mg SC Q8W: 1 injection of REGN3500 (30 mg total dose) plus 2 injections of REGN3500-matching placebo administered SC on day 1 and week 8; and 2 injections of REGN3500-matching placebo administered SC at weeks 2, 4, 6, 10, 12, and 14.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "6.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The 30 mg Q8W regimen only specifies active drug at day 1 and week 8, but the schedule for weeks 4 and 12 is missing (should be placebo injections to maintain blinding). This omission could lead to incorrect dosing.",
      "fix": "Specify the injections for weeks 4 and 12 for the 30 mg Q8W arm."
    },
    {
      "title": "Rescue treatment discontinuation rule conflicts with study design",
      "quote": "If rescue treatment consists of systemic corticosteroids or non-steroidal systemic immunosuppressive drugs, study treatment will be permanently discontinued immediately.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "6.5",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "This rule means patients receiving systemic rescue are permanently discontinued from study drug, but the protocol does not specify whether they remain in the study for follow-up. This could affect the analysis population and missing data handling.",
      "fix": "Define whether patients who discontinue study drug due to rescue treatment continue in the study for follow-up and how their data are handled."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing contraception requirements",
      "quote": "Male or female adult patients (≥18 to 75 years of age) with moderate-to-severe AD",
      "page": 7,
      "section": "5.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not specify contraception requirements for male and female patients of childbearing potential, which is essential for a study with an investigational drug.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed contraception section specifying acceptable methods, duration, and pregnancy testing requirements."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent study duration calculation",
      "quote": "Each patient’s participation in the study will be up to 53 weeks, including an up to 5-week (ie, 35 days) screening period, 16-week double-blind treatment period, and 20-week post-treatment follow-up period.",
      "page": 7,
      "section": "4.4",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "5 + 16 + 20 = 41 weeks, not 53 weeks. The 53-week figure is inconsistent with the sum of the stated periods.",
      "fix": "Correct the total study duration or explain the additional 12 weeks (e.g., if it includes a safety follow-up or other period)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Rescreening criteria vague",
      "quote": "Patients may be re-screened once if they fail the screening evaluation for reasons related to incidental transitory conditions (eg, medication use, concomitant illness, medical condition), unless the reason for the screen failure is related to failing the disease severity inclusion criteria.",
      "page": 6,
      "section": "5.6",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not specify the time window for rescreening or whether all screening assessments need to be repeated.",
      "fix": "Define the rescreening window and which assessments must be repeated."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing interim analysis details",
      "quote": "The safety and PK endpoints will not be included in the testing hierarchy.",
      "page": 9,
      "section": "10.9",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol mentions a testing hierarchy but does not describe any interim analyses, including whether they are planned, their timing, or the stopping rules. This is a critical omission for a dose-ranging study.",
      "fix": "Add a section on interim analyses, including any planned looks, alpha spending, and stopping rules."
    },
    {
      "title": "Incomplete sample size justification",
      "quote": "the enrollment of 60 patients per treatment group will provide 80% power to detect a 35% difference between the most efficacious REGN3500 SC dose and the placebo group",
      "page": 9,
      "section": "10.11",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size calculation only considers the most efficacious dose vs placebo, but the study has 4 active doses. No adjustment for multiple comparisons or consideration of dose-response modeling is described.",
      "fix": "Provide a more detailed sample size justification that accounts for the dose-ranging design and multiplicity."
    }
  ]
}
